result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.current_flow_betweenness_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Calculate current-flow (random-walk) betweenness for all nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L35973-L36052){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.current_flow_betweenness_centrality( normalized=True, weighted=None, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Current-flow betweenness centrality](/assets/graphs/current-flow-betweenness-centrality.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The shared seven-node graph shaded by current-flow betweenness, the share of electrical current through each node when every pair in turn injects and draws a unit of current. The bridge E carries the most at 0.58, then the hub C 0.43 and the tail node F 0.33; the pendant G carries none." width="100%"} Ordinary betweenness assumes everything travels along shortest paths. Current-flow betweenness (Newman 2005; Brandes & Fleischer 2005) instead treats the graph as an electrical network: for every pair of nodes, one unit of current enters at one and leaves at the other, spreading over *all* paths in proportion to their conductance, and a node's score is the total current passing through it. Equivalently, it counts how often a random walk between the pair passes through the node. This captures influence in networks where flow is not optimally routed (rumors, disease, power grids), and gives credit to nodes on near-shortest alternative routes, which shortest-path betweenness ignores. Edge weights act as conductances: heavier edges carry more current. The graph must be undirected and connected. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), divide by `(n - 1)(n - 2) / 2`, the number of pairs not involving the node, so scores lie in `[0, 1]`. Matches NetworkX. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights as conductances. If `None` (default), follows the graph (weights on `Graph(weighted=True)`). Weights must be positive. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute to store scores in. If `None` (default), uses `"current_flow_betweenness_centrality"`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores the scores as a node attribute and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: a dictionary mapping node IDs to scores. If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed or disconnected, or a weight is not positive. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a square with one diagonal, shortest-path betweenness gives the corners off the diagonal no credit, because the diagonal is always shortest. Current flow still sends some of the traffic around through them: ::: {#722fef29 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec square = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "A"), ("A", "C")]) ) label = square.get_label_from_id flow = square.current_flow_betweenness_centrality(return_dict=True) paths = square.betweenness_centrality(return_dict=True) {label(n): (round(flow[n], 3), round(paths[n], 3)) for n in sorted(flow)} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'A': (0.417, 0.167), 'B': (0.167, 0.0), 'C': (0.417, 0.167), 'D': (0.167, 0.0)} ``` ::: :::
